firstFive.what: A dark two-column money screen. Top left a $14.69 balance, under it a ring and the two things it is made of, under that what has happened to the money. Down the right what Bitcoin, Solana and Ether cost with a line each, what the assistant has been doing, a promise that nothing moves without a click, and a red STOP EVERYTHING.

firstFive.action: Read the balance and leave. When the assistant is asking, the question appears under the balance with YES, ALLOW IT and NO, and that becomes the one action

restamp:
Iteration 19 is a re-stamp, not a new change to the layout. The one file under ui/ this pass touched is ui/transition.js, the fall that dresses a mode change: sparse depth-tiered columns that start above the top edge so the fall arrives as a front, a five-row hot zone redrawn every frame through a white-hot luminance ramp, a bloom lifted off a seventh-scale buffer, and a ground that walks down the page instead of washing over it. Nothing in the DOM animates and no rule in style.css moved. Re-rendered and re-read at 1440, 768 and 390: the six regions sit where iteration 18 passed them, one page, no scrollbar.

The fall cannot be captured by this gate, because look.mjs enters a state by clicking and no control switches mode. Verified outside it by seizing requestAnimationFrame and stepping the run frame by frame, with captures across the cover, the hold, the reveal and the arriving half. 0.4ms median and 0.6ms p95 per frame at 1512x982, 151 frames, none dropped. Second pass on the same day: Karim saw a flicker, and it was mine. Re-rendering the hot zone every frame is right, rolling a NEW character into every one of those cells every frame is not, and about 675 glyphs were changing 60 times a second. Characters now belong to the row they were drawn on, kept in a small per-column ring, so only the colour and the alpha change from frame to frame; one row per column takes a new character with 8 percent odds, which is the shimmer. The glow marks are also snapped to whole buffer pixels, because a mark that small at a fractional offset pulses with its own antialiasing. Measured with the columns pinned still, so motion is out of the number: 53.4 percent of lit pixels changed between consecutive frames before, 1.3 percent after.
